terms.gloss: individual, one each, one by one; as a noun, individuals
terms.grammar: distributive adjective, plural; opposed to ūniversī, all together
evidence: Tac. Agr. 12.2: singulī pugnant, ūniversī vincuntur
Phaedr. 3 prol. 49: neque enim notāre singulōs mēns est mihi
Tac. Germ. 22.1: sēparātae singulīs sēdēs et sua cuique mēnsa
terms.comment: Each to their own is suus cuique: sua cuique mēnsa, individual tables.

terms.gloss: a private individual, a private citizen
terms.grammar: noun (the adjective prīvātus used as a noun)
evidence: Tac. H. 1.49: major prīvātō vīsus dum prīvātus fuit
terms.comment: The individual as against the state or an office-holder.

terms.grammar: adjective, with the genitive or dative
evidence: Quint. 11.3.18: propria cuique est (of each person’s voice)

terms.gloss: an individual (of a kind or species)
evidence: M-O s.v. individual: the sense marked medieval (Dante)
terms.comment: Classically “indivisible”: Cicero’s word for the atoms, indīvidua. The sense “an individual” belongs to medieval logic.

phrases.english: so they fight as individuals and are beaten as a whole

phrases.latin: neque enim notāre singulōs mēns est mihi, vērum ipsam vītam et mōrēs hominum ostendere
phrases.english: for I don’t mean to single out individuals, but to show life itself and the ways of people

phrases.latin: lautī cibum capiunt: sēparātae singulīs sēdēs et sua cuique mēnsa
phrases.english: when they have washed they eat, each at a separate seat and an individual table
